name: ReachTouch
summary: With hand tracking, extending the index finger shows a ray cursor on a distant target, and pushing the hand forward as if touching it selects the target, using the cursor position from just before the push.
howItWorks: Built for Meta Quest 3 hand tracking. A small neural network (MLP) recognises the pointing hand pose and shows a cursor only while the index finger is extended; an LSTM detects the forward touch motion. Because the push moves the cursor, the system selects at the cursor position recorded just before the push began. In a study with 16 participants on a panel 2 m away, ReachTouch was 26.5% faster than hand raycasting with pinch (35.2% for the smallest targets), with fewer errors in some conditions and a higher SUS score. It was not yet tested with 3D objects.
advantages: Touch-like confirmation that does not shift the cursor the way a pinch can.
limitations: Evaluated only on a flat panel at a fixed distance; 3D objects and multiple panels remain to be tested.

relationships.note: Compared with hand raycasting confirmed by a pinch.
